      document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
        (function () {
          //lazy load images code are used here
          var lazyloadImages;
          var lazyloadSection;
          if ("IntersectionObserver" in window) {
            lazyloadImages = document.querySelectorAll(".lazy");
            lazyloadSection = document.querySelectorAll(".category-block");
            var imageObserver = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries, observer) {
              entries.forEach(function (entry) {
                if (entry.isIntersecting) {
                  var image = entry.target;
                  image.src = image.dataset.src;
                  image.classList.remove("lazy");
                  imageObserver.unobserve(image);
                } else {
                  //console.log(entry)
                }
              });
            });
            var sectionObserver = new IntersectionObserver(function (entries, observer) {
              entries.forEach(function (entry) {
                if (entry.isIntersecting) {
                  var section = entry.target;
                  section.children[0].dataset.categorySection = 'show'
                  sectionObserver.unobserve(section);

                } else {
                  // console.log(entry)
                }

              });
            });
            lazyloadImages.forEach(function (image) {
              imageObserver.observe(image);
              //console.log(imageObserver)
            });
            lazyloadSection.forEach(function (entry) {
              sectionObserver.observe(entry);
              //console.log(sectionObserver)
            });
          } else {
            var lazyloadThrottleTimeout;
            lazyloadImages = document.querySelectorAll(".lazy");
            lazyloadSection = document.querySelectorAll(".category-block");
            function lazyload() {
              if (lazyloadThrottleTimeout) {
                clearTimeout(lazyloadThrottleTimeout);
              }
              lazyloadThrottleTimeout = setTimeout(function () {
                var scrollTop = window.pageYOffset;
                lazyloadImages.forEach(function (img) {
                  if (img.offsetTop < (window.innerHeight + scrollTop)) {
                    img.src = img.dataset.src;
                    img.classList.remove('lazy');
                  }
                });
                if (lazyloadSection.length !== 0) {
                  lazyloadSection.forEach(function (section) {
                    if (section.offsetTop < (window.innerHeight + scrollTop)) {
                      if (section.children[0].dataset.categorySection !== 'show') {
                        section.children[0].dataset.categorySection = 'show'
                      }
                    }
                  });
                }
                if (lazyloadImages.length == 0) {
                  document.removeEventListener("scroll", lazyload);
                  window.removeEventListener("resize", lazyload);
                  window.removeEventListener("orientationChange", lazyload);
                }
              }, 20);
            }

            document.addEventListener("scroll", lazyload);
            window.addEventListener("resize", lazyload);
            window.addEventListener("orientationChange", lazyload);
          }
          //lazy load images code are included here
        })();
      });
    </script>

            <h1 itemprop="headline" class="title">Odisha bandh: Congress holds torch rally ahead of bandh; police deploy 150 officers for security</h1>
            <div class="d-flex justify-content-between align-items-center">

            <p class="time"><span class="time-gray">
                <span itemprop="author creator" itemscope="" itemtype="http://schema.org/Person">
                    <span itemprop="name">ANI |</span>
                </span> Updated: </span><span class="time-red" itemprop="dateModified"><span class="first">Oct</span> 08, 2026 08:13 </span><span class="first red-ist"> IST</span>
            </p>
            <a href="https://google.com/preferences/source?q=aninews.in" target="_blank" class="mb-4 hidden-xs">
                <img src="https://d3lzcn6mbbadaf.cloudfront.net/static/img/ani-trusted-btn-white.png" alt="ani-trusted-source" class="ani-trusted-source" style="width: 120px;">

        <div class="hidden-md hidden-lg hidden-xl">
            <a target="_blank" class="green-btn" href="https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029Va7q7004dTnMVl9H9r0o">ANI News

        <div class="content count-br" itemprop="articleBody">
            <span class="custom-br"></span><p>Bhubaneswar (Odisha) [India], October 8 (ANI): The Odisha Congress organised a torch rally ahead of the <a href="/topic/odisha-bandh">Odisha bandh</a> called by the Congress and INDIA bloc, while the Bhubaneswar-Cuttack Police Commissionerate said around 150 officers would be deployed to maintain law and order during the shutdown on Thursday.<span class="custom-br"></span>Odisha Congress president Bhakta Charan Das appealed to people to support the bandh, describing it as a fight to protect constitutional and land rights.<span class="custom-br"></span>“I humbly appeal to the people of Odisha to support our democratic Bandh tomorrow. This is a fight to protect our constitutional rights and the rights over our land,” Das said on Wednesday.<span class="custom-br"></span></p><div class="bpcl-inline" data-bpcl-inline="">
						<div class="bpcl-slide is-active">
							<a href="https://www.bharatpetroleum.in/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" id="news-ad-1" data-gtm-vis-polling-id7618942_57="59">
								<img src="https://d3lzcn6mbbadaf.cloudfront.net/static/img/ads/2026/jul/bpcl-mak-car-leaderboard.jpg" alt="BPCL MAK lubricants" width="2048" height="254">
							</a>
						</div>
						<div class="bpcl-slide">
							<a href="https://www.bharatpetroleum.in/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" id="news-ad-2" data-gtm-vis-polling-id7618942_58="60">
								<img src="https://d3lzcn6mbbadaf.cloudfront.net/static/img/ads/2026/jul/bpcl-mak-bike-leaderboard.jpg" alt="BPCL MAK lubricants" width="2048" height="254">
							</a>
						</div>
						<button type="button" class="bpcl-nav bpcl-prev" data-bpcl-prev="" aria-label="Previous advertisement">‹</button>
						<button type="button" class="bpcl-nav bpcl-next" data-bpcl-next="" aria-label="Next advertisement">›</button>
					</div><p>He also appealed to party workers to ensure that the shutdown remained peaceful and democratic while respecting the law.<span class="custom-br"></span>Odisha Pradesh Congress Committee Vice President Santosh Singh Saluja appealed to people to cooperate with the bandh and alleged that democracy was being undermined through “vote theft”.<span class="custom-br"></span>“The Congress and INDIA bloc have called for a bandh in Odisha tomorrow. We appeal to every individual to cooperate tomorrow and make the bandh a success. In the country, the republic is being murdered through vote theft,” Saluja said.<span class="custom-br"></span>Meanwhile, Bhubaneswar-Cuttack Police Commissioner Suresh Devdutt Singh on Wednesday said extensive security arrangements had been made for the bandh.<span class="custom-br"></span>“Several opposition parties called for an <a href="/topic/odisha-bandh">Odisha bandh</a> tomorrow, which also includes our Bhubaneswar-Cuttack region. Extensive police arrangements have been made to maintain law and order during this bandh tomorrow,” he said.<span class="custom-br"></span>The Police Commissioner said efforts had been made to ensure that demonstrations remained peaceful and within the constitutional and legal framework.<span class="custom-br"></span><img class="img-responsive" src="https://aniportalimages.s3.amazonaws.com/media/details/ANI-20261008022500.jpg" alt=""><span class="custom-br"></span>“Special arrangements have been made, in particular, to ensure the smooth functioning of the national highway, railway lines, and all such routes. Around 150 officers will be deployed for this,” he said.<span class="custom-br"></span>He said the police would ensure that essential services were not affected and that people did not face difficulties in accessing hospitals and other necessary services.<span class="custom-br"></span>The Commissioner appealed to political parties to exercise their democratic rights peacefully and within the law, adding that maintaining peace was the responsibility of the police.<span class="custom-br"></span>Meanwhile, the bandh call is being observed in Sambalpur on Thursday and is likely to affect normal life across the city, with markets, schools and colleges remaining closed.<span class="custom-br"></span>The bandh is also likely to affect operations at Sambalpur Railway Station, where Congress workers reportedly stopped the Sambalpur-Puri train as part of their protest.<span class="custom-br"></span>Congress leaders and workers were seen participating in the bandh and appealing to people and business establishments to support the shutdown. (ANI)</p>
        </div>

    <script>
      document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
        const AUTO_SUGGEST_URL = "/web-auto-suggestions/";
        const queryInput = document.querySelector('[data-query]');
        const suggestionsBox = document.querySelector('[data-suggestions-box]');
        const form = queryInput.closest('form'); // find the parent form of the input

        queryInput.addEventListener('input', async () => {
          const query = queryInput.value.trim();
          if (query.length < 2) {
            suggestionsBox.innerHTML = '';
            suggestionsBox.classList.add('hidden');
            return;
          }

          try {
            const res = await fetch(`${AUTO_SUGGEST_URL}?query=${encodeURIComponent(query)}`);
            const data = await res.json();
            if (data.status && Array.isArray(data.data)) {
              showSuggestions(data.data, query);
            } else {
              suggestionsBox.innerHTML = '';
              suggestionsBox.classList.add('hidden');
            }
          } catch (err) {
            console.error(err);
            suggestionsBox.innerHTML = '';
            suggestionsBox.classList.add('hidden');
          }
        });

        function escapeHtml(text) {
          return text
            .replace(/&/g, '&')
            .replace(/</g, '<')
            .replace(/>/g, '>')
            .replace(/\"/g, '"')
            .replace(/'/g, ''');
        }

        function highlightMatch(text, query) {
          const escapedText = escapeHtml(text);
          if (!query) return escapedText;
          const escapedQueryForRegex = query.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');
          const regex = new RegExp(`(${escapedQueryForRegex})`, 'ig');
          return escapedText.replace(regex, '<span style="font-weight:bold">$1</span>');
        }

        function showSuggestions(suggestions, query) {
          suggestionsBox.innerHTML = '';
          suggestions.forEach(suggestion => {
            const li = document.createElement('li');
            li.innerHTML = highlightMatch(suggestion, query);
            li.className = 'suggestion-list cursor-pointer px-2 py-1 hover:bg-gray-100';
            li.addEventListener('click', () => {
              queryInput.value = suggestion;
              suggestionsBox.classList.add('hidden');
              if (form) form.submit(); // submit the form on click
            });
            suggestionsBox.appendChild(li);
          });
          suggestionsBox.classList.remove('hidden');
        }

        document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
          if (!suggestionsBox.contains(e.target) && e.target !== queryInput) {
            suggestionsBox.classList.add('hidden');
          }
        });
      });
    </script>

    <script>
      var current_fs, next_fs, previous_fs, animate = false; //fieldsets
      var left, opacity, scale; //fieldset properties which we will animate
      $("[data-next-news-new]").click(function () {
        if (!animate && $(this).is('.active')) {
          animate = true;
          var $this = $(this);
          current_fs = $(this).parents('.right-block').find('.tab.active');
          next_fs = current_fs.next();
          if (next_fs.is('.tab')) {
            next_fs.show().css({ 'display': 'block' });
            current_fs.animate({ opacity: 0 }, {
              step: function (now, mx) {
                scale = 1 - (1 - now) * 0.2;
                //2. bring next_fs from the right(50%)
                left = (now * 50) + "%";
                //3. increase opacity of next_fs to 1 as it moves in
                opacity = 1 - now;
                // console.log(now,scale,left,opacity);
                current_fs.css({
                  'transform': 'scale(' + scale + ')',
                  'position': 'absolute'
                });
                next_fs.css({ 'left': left, 'opacity': opacity });
              },
              duration: 800,
              complete: function () {
                animate = false;

                current_fs.hide().removeClass('active');
                next_fs.addClass('active');
                if (!next_fs.next().is('.tab')) {
                  $this.removeClass('active')
                } else {
                  $this.prev().is('.active') ? '' : $this.prev().addClass('active');
                }
              }
            });
          }
        }
      });
      $("[data-prev-news-new]").click(function () {
        if (!animate && $(this).is('.active')) {
          animate = true;
          var $this = $(this);
          current_fs = $(this).parents('.right-block').find('.tab.active');
          previous_fs = current_fs.prev();
          if (previous_fs.is('.tab')) {
            previous_fs.show().css({ 'display': 'block' });;

            current_fs.animate({ opacity: 0 }, {
              step: function (now, mx) {
                scale = 0.8 + (1 - now) * 0.2;
                left = ((1 - now) * 50) + "%";
                opacity = 1 - now;
                current_fs.css({ 'left': left });
                previous_fs.css({ 'transform': 'scale(' + scale + ')', 'opacity': opacity, });
              },
              duration: 800,
              complete: function () {
                animate = false;
                current_fs.hide().removeClass('active');
                previous_fs.addClass('active');
                previous_fs.css({ 'position': 'relative', });

                if (!previous_fs.prev().is('.tab')) {
                  $this.removeClass('active')
                } else {
                  $this.next().is('.active') ? '' : $this.next().addClass('active');
                }
              }
            });
          }

        }
      });

    "articleBody" : "Bhubaneswar: The Biju Janata Dal (BJD) on Wednesday made a dramatic U-turn on the Congress’s call for a 12-hour Odisha bandh on Thursday, exposing the regional party’s dilemma over its ties with the Opposition camp.    The reversal came barely 30 minutes after senior BJD leader Pramila Mallik announced that the party would support the bandh against the alleged deletion of voters’ names from electoral rolls during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).    Mallik first told reporters around noon that the BJD would join the Congress-sponsored shutdown, citing the participation of the party’s Rajya Sabha members in the INDIA bloc’s protest march in New Delhi against the SIR exercise.    However, within half an hour, Mallik called another press conference at her residence and clarified that the BJD would not support or participate in the Odisha bandh.    She also sought to draw a distinction between the BJD’s participation in the INDIA bloc’s Delhi protest and any formal association with the Opposition alliance.    “Recently, we held an economic blockade in Sundargarh. Did anyone support us then? Wherever the interests of the people or the State are harmed, our beloved leader (Naveen Patnaik) has fought and the Biju Janata Dal has fought. We will stand by that fight. Whether any party supports us or not, we will maintain equal distance. We have neither joined any alliance nor supported any political party,” Mallik said.    Her clarification appeared aimed at reinforcing the BJD’s long-standing claim that it maintains equidistance from both the BJP and the Congress.    Earlier in the day, however, Mallik had taken a distinctly different position.    “Our party (BJD) has extended support, and we have already protested against the Election Commission of India’s actions, particularly the alleged wrongful removal of voters from the electoral rolls. Therefore, we will support tomorrow’s strike and extend our full support to the movement,” she had said.    The two statements, delivered within a short interval, have raised questions about the BJD’s political positioning at a time when the party has shown signs of greater engagement with the Congress-led Opposition on certain issues.    The BJD’s Rajya Sabha members had on Tuesday participated in the INDIA bloc’s protest march in Delhi against the SIR exercise. The move had fuelled speculation about whether the regional party was gradually moving closer to the Opposition grouping despite repeatedly asserting that it had not joined the alliance.      According to political analyst Sriram Dash, the party’s decision to back away from Thursday’s bandh indicates that it remains keen to preserve its independent political identity in Odisha.      ",

			"articleBody": "Bhubaneswar A dawn-to-dusk Odisha Bandh called by INDIA Bloc parties to protest the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026, and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over his involvement in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls evoked a mixed response on Thursday (October 8, 2026). INDIA Bloc parties, including the Congress and Left parties, were seen enforcing the bandh on the streets of Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Berhampur and all major district headquarters towns. The parties had made it clear that ambulances and students travelling for examinations would be kept out of the purview of the bandh. BJD distances itself from Congress after withdrawing support for Odisha Bandh BJD distances itself from Congress after withdrawing support for Odisha Bandh Senior BJD leader and party Chief Whip Pramila Mallik backtracked on Odisha Bandh support within an hour after initially extending support for INDIA Bloc\u2019s call for Bandh on Thursday BJD distances itself from Congress after withdrawing support for Odisha Bandh storyline 1 However, business establishments remained closed along national and state highways and major arterial roads in the towns. There were no reports of violence, except for protesters halting passenger vehicles and enquiring about their destinations. As long-distance buses were parked safely at bus terminals in view of the shutdown, passengers were seen waiting for the impact of the bandh to ease. MoEF grants environmental, CRZ clearance for Puri\u2019s greenfield airport MoEF grants environmental, CRZ clearance for Puri\u2019s greenfield airport MoEF directs to prepare a bird hazard study from reputed institute in the field after a Wildlife Institute of India study flags the issue of risk posed by migratory birds from Chilika Lake MoEF grants environmental, CRZ clearance for Puri\u2019s greenfield airport storyline 1 \u201cThe Odisha Bandh observed on October 8 received an unprecedented response across the State, with the constituent parties of the INDIA Bloc coming together in Bhubaneswar to stage a strong and united protest,\u201d said Suresh Panigrahy, State secretary of the CPI(M). Mr Panigrahy said the CEC must step down after massive irregularities in the SIR exercise came to light and the entire country stood up against the Election Commission of India, whose credibility, he said, was now at an all-time low. \u201cAs far as Odisha is concerned, the MMDR Amendment Act has snatched away the State\u2019s right to impose tax on mineral extraction from its land. It will badly hit the economy of a mineral-rich State like Odisha in the long run,\u201d he pointed out. Protesters also demanded the resignation of School and Mass Education Minister Nityanand Gond over more than 1,700 errors detected in school textbooks prepared for Classes I to VIII. INDIA Bloc parties warned that their protest against alleged irregularities and what they described as anti-democratic steps by the BJP governments at the State and Centre would not end with the Odisha Bandh and would continue in the future.",

</h1><h2 class="sub-title" style="font-family: 'Merriweather', serif; font-weight: bold;">Business establishments, petrol pumps, shops and many educational institutes were seen closed in the morning, while public transport such as buses and autorickshaws remained off the road</h2><div class="update-publish-time"><p class="updated-time">Updated <span> - October 17, 2026 07:47 am IST - Bhubaneswar</span></p></div><div class="author"><div class="author-name noimg"><a href="https://www.thehindu.com/profile/author/the-hindu-bureau-14355/" class="person-name lnk"> The Hindu Bureau</a></div></div><div class="comments-shares share-page flex print-hide" data-artid="71558469" data-title="Odisha bandh by INDIA Bloc evokes mixed response" data-url="https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/odisha/normal-life-hit-in-odisha-as-india-bloc-parties-observe-bandh-over-new-mining-law-other-issues/article71558469.ece"><div class="left"><button class="btn comments" data-ga-labelclick="OpenComments"><span class="coral-count" data-coral-url="https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/odisha/normal-life-hit-in-odisha-as-india-bloc-parties-observe-bandh-over-new-mining-law-other-issues/article71558469.ece" data-coral-id="71558469" data-coral-notext="true"></span></button><div class="read-later"><button class="btn read-later-btn" data-articleid="71558469" style="display: block;" data-ga-labelclick="ReadLater"><span>READ LATER</span></button><div class="delete-tool-tip" style="display: none;"><a class="cancel" href="https://www.thehindu.com/myaccount/?tab=bookmarks">
                SEE ALL         
                </a><span class="delete bookmarkdelete">
                    Remove     
                </span></div></div></div><div class="right"><div id="article-top-right"></div></div></div><div class="article-picture top-pic "><div class="picture verticle"><picture><!--[if IE 9]><video style="display: none;"><![endif]--><source media="(min-width: 1600px)" sizes="960px" srcset="https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/cyu06k/article71558490.ece/alternates/LANDSCAPE_1200/PTI09_29_2026_000302A.jpg"><source media="(min-width: 768px) and (max-width: 1599px)" sizes="640px" srcset="https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/cyu06k/article71558490.ece/alternates/LANDSCAPE_1200/PTI09_29_2026_000302A.jpg"><source media="(min-width: 321px) and (max-width: 767px)" sizes="400px" srcset="https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/cyu06k/article71558490.ece/alternates/LANDSCAPE_660/PTI09_29_2026_000302A.jpg"><source media="(max-width: 320px)" sizes="320px" srcset="https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/cyu06k/article71558490.ece/alternates/LANDSCAPE_320/PTI09_29_2026_000302A.jpg"><!--[if IE 9]></video><![endif]--><img src="https://www.thehindu.com/theme/images/th-online/1x1_spacer.png" alt="Congress-led INDIA bloc workers and leaders stage a protest rally against the MMDR Amendment Act, in Bhubaneswar, September 29, 2026." title="Congress-led INDIA bloc workers and leaders stage a protest rally against the MMDR Amendment Act, in Bhubaneswar, September 29, 2026." data-original="https://www.thehindu.com/theme/images/th-online/1x1_spacer.png" class="lead-img" fetchpriority="high"></picture></div><p class="caption">
                    Congress-led INDIA bloc workers and leaders stage a protest rally against the MMDR Amendment Act, in Bhubaneswar, September 29, 2026.
                                          | Photo Credit: PTI
                                      </p></div><div id="content-body-71558469" class="articlebodycontent col-xl-9 col-lg-12 col-md-12 col-sm-12 col-12"><div class="schemaDiv" id="schemaDiv"><p>A dawn-to-dusk Odisha Bandh called by INDIA Bloc parties to protest the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026, and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over his involvement in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls evoked a mixed response on Thursday (October 8, 2026).</p><div class="article-ad"><div class="dfp-ad articleinlinead  middleonead" id="Desktop_AT_Mid01" style="min-height: 90px;"></div></div><p>INDIA Bloc parties, including the Congress and Left parties, were seen enforcing the bandh on the streets of Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Berhampur and all major district headquarters towns. The parties had made it clear that ambulances and students travelling for examinations would be kept out of the purview of the bandh.</p><div class="" id="artmeterpv"></div><div class="also-read print-hide" data-ga-label="AlsoReadArticle"><div class="element"><div class="title"><a href="https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/odisha/bjd-distances-itself-from-congress-after-withdrawing-support-for-odisha-bandh/article71556470.ece">
										BJD distances itself from Congress after withdrawing support for Odisha Bandh</a></div><div class="picture"><img src="https://www.thehindu.com/theme/images/th-online/1x1_spacer.png" data-src-template="https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/8h9iwq/article71558294.ece/alternates/SQUARE_80/OD-TEXBOOKS-PATGF4G6F270.3.jpg.jpg" data-original="https://th-i.thgim.com/public/incoming/8h9iwq/article71558294.ece/alternates/SQUARE_80/OD-TEXBOOKS-PATGF4G6F270.3.jpg.jpg" alt="" data-device-variant="SQUARE~SQUARE~SQUARE~SQUARE" class="media-object lazy adaptive placeholder lazy" width="100%" height="100%"></div></div></div><p>However, business establishments remained closed along national and state highways and major arterial roads in the towns. There were no reports of violence, except for protesters halting passenger vehicles and enquiring about their destinations.</p><div class="article-ad"><div class="dfp-ad articleinlinead" id="Desktop_Inarticle_1x1" style="min-height: 250px;"></div></div><p>As long-distance buses were parked safely at bus terminals in view of the shutdown, passengers were seen waiting for the impact of the bandh to ease.</p><div class="also-read print-hide" data-ga-label="AlsoReadArticle"><div class="element"><div class="title"><a href="https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/odisha/moef-grants-environmental-crz-clearance-for-puris-greenfield-airport/article71556220.ece">
										MoEF grants environmental, CRZ clearance for Puri’s greenfield airport</a></div><div class="picture"></div></div></div><p>“The Odisha Bandh observed on October 8 received an unprecedented response across the State, with the constituent parties of the INDIA Bloc coming together in Bhubaneswar to stage a strong and united protest,” said Suresh Panigrahy, State secretary of the CPI(M).</p><p>Mr Panigrahy said the CEC must step down after massive irregularities in the SIR exercise came to light and the entire country stood up against the Election Commission of India, whose credibility, he said, was now at an all-time low.</p><div class="article-ad"><div class="dfp-ad articleinlinead" id="Desktop_AT_Mid02" style="min-height: 90px;"></div></div><p>“As far as Odisha is concerned, the MMDR Amendment Act has snatched away the State’s right to impose tax on mineral extraction from its land. It will badly hit the economy of a mineral-rich State like Odisha in the long run,” he pointed out.</p><p>Protesters also demanded the resignation of School and Mass Education Minister Nityanand Gond over more than 1,700 errors detected in school textbooks prepared for Classes I to VIII. INDIA Bloc parties warned that their protest against alleged irregularities and what they described as anti-democratic steps by the BJP governments at the State and Centre would not end with the Odisha Bandh and would continue in the future.</p></div><div class="articleblock-container" id="arthardpv"></div><div class="update-publish-time article-published-time-end"><p class="publish-time-new"> Published <span>- October 08, 2026 10:57 am IST</span></p></div><button class="btn comments comment-btn print-hide">

several districts of Odisha on Thursday as INDIA bloc parties observed a 12-hour bandh from 6 am to 6 pm to protest the new mining law, alleged errors in school textbooks and alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Supporters of the Congress, CPI, CPI(M), CPI(ML) Liberation, Forward Bloc, NCP (Sharad Pawar), Samajwadi Party, RJD and JMM staged demonstrations and blocked roads at several places, including Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Bargarh, Bhadrak, Balasore, Rayagada, Kendrapara, Bolangir, Berhampur and Sambalpur.Protesters also stopped buses, trucks, taxis and autorickshaws at several locations and burnt tyres, disrupting traffic movement.Shops, business establishments, petrol pumps and several educational institutions remained closed in parts of the state, while public transport services were hit.Many commuters were left waiting at bus stops, with office-goers, students and others facing difficulties in reaching their destinations. Auto-rickshaw services were also affected in some areas.In Bhubaneswar, the Capital Region Urban Transport (CRUT) said Ama Bus services were intended to operate, though services on some routes could be affected depending on the situation.Essential services, including hospitals, ambulances, fire services, pharmacies and milk supply, were kept outside the purview of the bandh, a Congress leader said.The INDIA bloc has demanded the repeal of the MMDR (Amendment) Act, the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged "vote chori" and the resignation of state minister Nityananda Gond over alleged errors in school textbooks."We demand a complete rollback of the MMDR (Amendment) Act, resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar for 'vote chori' and state minister Nityananda Gond for distributing books with erroneous information among school students," senior Congress leader Suresh Routray said in Bhubaneswar.Police deployed adequate security across the state to prevent any untoward incidents and said efforts were being made to ensure that the demonstrations remained peaceful and within the ambit of constitutional rights.Bhubaneswar-Cuttack Police Commissioner S Dev Dutta Singh said, "Discussions have been held with various stakeholders so that protesters conduct their demonstrations within the ambit of their constitutional rights."- <div id="postexcerpt"><p>Bhubaneswar, Oct 7 (PTI) The Naveen Patnaik-led BJD on Wednesday decided to stay away from the Odisha bandh called by INDIA bloc parties on October 8 against the new mining law, errors in school textbooks and the SIR exercise, asserting that it would remain equidistant from the BJP-led NDA and Congress-led opposition alliance.</p><div class="code-block code-block-5" style="margin: 8px 0; clear: both;">
<div id="vdo_ai_div"></div><script>(function(v,d,o,ai){ai=d.createElement('script');ai.defer=true;ai.async=true;ai.src=v.location.protocol+o;d.head.appendChild(ai);})(window, document, '//a.vdo.ai/core/theprint/vdo.ai.js');</script></div>
<p>The decision came a day after BJD leaders joined an opposition protest in Delhi seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.<div id="74b3e53b-d5c7-4bcb-955f-27ffce21ecdd" data-section="74b3e53b-d5c7-4bcb-955f-27ffce21ecdd" class="_ap_apex_ad" data-xpath="#postexcerpt > p:eq(1)" data-section-id="" data-ap-network="adpTags" style="display: block; clear: both; text-align: center; margin: 30px auto 10px; width: 336px; height: 280px; overflow: hidden;" data-render-time="1795345468745">

	</div>
	</div></p><div class="code-block code-block-16" style="margin: 8px 0; clear: both;">

<div class="third-para"><p>The 12-hour bandh, called by nine parties of the INDIA bloc for Thursday, is also demanding the resignation of Odisha School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond over alleged errors in school textbooks.</p>
				<button id="examples-expand" class="ap-m-clip-expand">
				<span>
					Show Full Article
					<svg class="ap-m-clip-expand-icon" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" height="1em" viewBox="0 0 320 512"><path d="M143 352.3L7 216.3c-9.4-9.4-9.4-24.6 0-33.9l22.6-22.6c9.4-9.4 24.6-9.4 33.9 0l96.4 96.4 96.4-96.4c9.4-9.4 24.6-9.4 33.9 0l22.6 22.6c9.4 9.4 9.4 24.6 0 33.9l-136 136c-9.2 9.4-24.4 9.4-33.8 0z"></path></svg>

<script data-nopdlab="true">
/*for Font resize*/
$('document').ready(function(){
	var cookie = "fontsize";

	var getFontSize = function(){
		var value = parseInt($.cookie(cookie))
	  return  value||20;
	}

	var changeFontSize = function(direction){
	  var newSize = Math.min(24, Math.max(16, getFontSize()+direction))
	  $.cookie(cookie, newSize, {expires: 30, path: '/', domain  : ''});
	  updateFontSize(newSize)
	}
	var updateFontSize = function(fontsize){
	  var style = $('#font_size_style')
	  if(!style.length){
		style = $('<style id="font_size_style">')
		$(document.body).append(style)
	  }
	  style.text(".td-post-content p { font-size: "+fontsize+"px; line-height: "+(fontsize + 10)+"px;}")
	}

	var initFontSize = function(){
	  var fontsize = getFontSize()
	  console.log(fontsize)
	  updateFontSize(fontsize)
	}

	$(document).ready(initFontSize); 

	$('#td-outer-wrap').on( "click", "#up", function() {        
	  changeFontSize(1)
	});

	$('#td-outer-wrap').on( "click", "#down", function() {
	  changeFontSize(-1)
	}); 
});
</script>

// Dropdown Menu Logic using clean semantic CSS classes
const shareButton = document.getElementById('shareButton');
const shareDropdown = document.getElementById('shareDropdown');
let isDropdownOpen = false;

function toggleDropdown(forceState) {
    isDropdownOpen = forceState !== undefined ? forceState : !isDropdownOpen;
    
    if (isDropdownOpen) {
        shareDropdown.classList.add('is-visible');
        // Small delay to allow display:block to apply before triggering CSS transition
        setTimeout(() => {
            shareDropdown.classList.add('dropdown-enter-active');
        }, 10);
        shareButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
        shareButton.classList.add('is-active');
    } else {
        shareDropdown.classList.remove('dropdown-enter-active');
        shareDropdown.classList.remove('is-visible');
        shareButton.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
        shareButton.classList.remove('is-active');
    }
}

// Toggle on button click
shareButton.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    e.stopPropagation();
    toggleDropdown();
});

// Close dropdown when clicking outside
document.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    if (isDropdownOpen && !shareDropdown.contains(e.target) && e.target !== shareButton) {
        toggleDropdown(false);
    }
});

// Prevent closing when clicking inside the dropdown itself
shareDropdown.addEventListener('click', (e) => {
    e.stopPropagation();
});

// Copy Link to Clipboard function
function copyToClipboard() {
    const url = window.location.href;
    const textArea = document.createElement("textarea");
    textArea.value = url;
    textArea.style.position = "fixed";
    document.body.appendChild(textArea);
    textArea.focus();
    textArea.select();
    try {
        document.execCommand('copy');
        showToast('Link copied to clipboard!');
    } catch (err) {
        console.error('Unable to copy link', err);
    }
    document.body.removeChild(textArea);
    toggleDropdown(false);
}

// Toast notification helper
function showToast(message) {
    const toast = document.createElement('div');
    toast.textContent = message;
    toast.className = 'toast-notification';
    document.body.appendChild(toast);
    
    setTimeout(() => {
        toast.style.opacity = '0';
        setTimeout(() => document.body.removeChild(toast), 300);
    }, 3000);
